name: Primary Effusion Lymphoma

ethnicAssociations: More common in Mediterranean and East Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Effusion Lymphoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant lymphomatous effusions in body cavities without detectable tumor masses
Expression of B-cell markers (often CD45+, CD30+, CD38+, CD138+) with absence or weak expression of typical B-cell markers (CD20, CD79a)
Detection of Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) latent nuclear antigen in tumor cells
Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) positivity in some cases (supportive but not required)
Cytological identification of large atypical lymphoid cells with plasmablastic or immunoblastic morphology in effusion fluid

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of malignant effusions without tumor masses, HHV-8 positivity in tumor cells, and characteristic immunophenotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other lymphomas and carcinomas causing effusions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Malignant pleural, pericardial, or peritoneal effusions without detectable masses
pathognomonic.notes: Effusions may be hemorrhagic and recurrent
May cause tamponade or respiratory compromise

common.symptomName: Constitutional B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Dyspnea due to pleural or pericardial effusion

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to CNS involvement
rare.notes: Very rare; usually indicates advanced disease

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to tumor lysis or effusion-related complications

laboratory: Cytology of effusion fluid showing large atypical lymphoid cells
Immunophenotyping positive for CD45, CD30, CD38, CD138; negative or weak CD20
HHV-8 latent nuclear antigen detected by immunohistochemistry or PCR
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing pleural, pericardial, or peritoneal effusions without solid masses
Ultrasound or CT confirming absence of lymphadenopathy or tumor masses
genetic: HHV-8 viral genome detection in tumor cells
other: Exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes and metastatic carcinoma
Frequent association with HIV infection or immunosuppression

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of characteristic vascular spindle cell tumors
HHV-8 positive but no malignant lymphoid effusions
Usually presents with solid tumor masses
Malignant pleural or peritoneal tumors of mesothelial origin
Cytology shows mesothelial cells, not lymphoid cells

redFlags: Rapidly accumulating malignant effusions causing respiratory or cardiac compromise
HHV-8 positivity in effusion lymphoid cells
Failure to respond to standard lymphoma therapies
Presence of B symptoms with unexplained effusions
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2017
Knowles DM. Primary effusion lymphoma: a distinct clinicopathologic entity associated with HHV-8. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 1997
Cesarman E. Primary effusion lymphoma: a distinct clinicopathologic entity associated with HHV-8. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2012
